description:
Soar Duo is passionate about science, technology, space, environmental innovation and creative problem-solving. For the 2026 NASA Space Apps Challenge, we're building the Delhi Air Jukebox an interactive experience that transforms real air-quality data into sound, helping people understand the impact of pollution during Diwali.

We're looking for skills in coding, data science, UI/UX design, environmental science, music and scientific research who want to turn data into meaningful change!
summary:
Endangered Air is an interactive Earth Jukebox that transforms real atmospheric observations into an immersive audiovisual experience, helping people hear what is happening in the air they breathe. Focusing on two monitoring locations in New Delhi during the 2026 Diwali period, the application combines NASA Earth resources with historical environmental data from the Meteomatics API to create synchronized maps, charts, and real-time sonification. Every sound is generated directly from measured environmental variables using transparent, repeatable mappings—turning changes in temperature, wind, humidity, pressure, cloud cover, and precipitation into music that evolves with the data. By making invisible environmental changes both visible and audible, **Endangered Air** offers an engaging, accessible, and educational way to explore Earth observations, demonstrating how sound can complement traditional scientific visualization and inspire greater awareness of our changing planet.

Hear the Planet. Understand the Danger.
details:
Endangered Air is an interactive Earth Jukebox that transforms Earth observations into an immersive audiovisual experience. Inspired by NASA's Earth Information Center (EIC), the application combines NASA Earth visualizations with real atmospheric observations to help people explore environmental change through both sight and sound.

Our featured experience focuses on New Delhi, allowing users to compare atmospheric conditions between Chandni Chowk and Lodhi Road over time. Interactive maps, synchronized charts, timelines, and procedural audio reveal how weather and atmospheric conditions evolve, making complex Earth science more engaging, intuitive, and accessible.

The application retrieves historical environmental observations using the Meteomatics Weather API and pairs them with NASA Earth Information Center resources. Environmental variables—including temperature, humidity, wind speed, wind direction, atmospheric pressure, cloud cover, and precipitation—are deterministically mapped to musical elements such as melody, rhythm, harmony, texture, and timbre. Identical observations always produce identical sound, ensuring transparency, repeatability, and explainable sonification.

Users can explore NASA Earth stories, compare locations, adjust audio layers, replay time periods, and experience synchronized visual and audio playback through an accessible interface designed for learners, educators, researchers, and the public. Endangered Air demonstrates how sonification can complement traditional scientific visualization, making Earth science more inclusive and engaging for everyone.

Technology Stack

  • React + TypeScript
  • Vite
  • Tone.js & Web Audio API
  • Tailwind CSS + shadcn/ui
  • Recharts
  • TanStack Query
  • Meteomatics Weather API
  • NASA Earth Information Center (EIC) resources
  • GitHub
  • Lovable.dev

The Earth Stories page plays sound from 11 official NASA Scientific Visualization Studio visualizations. Two of them come from the sources you listed:

  • GEOS Aerosols (NASA's atmospheric aerosol visualization) is one of the playable stories.
  • Data Sonification: Caldwell 73 is used as the method reference on the Sonification page and is listed on the Sources page.

Two of your sources are only partly covered:

  • NASA Earth Information Center: its original Earth Now video is no longer online, so that story uses NASA's near-surface temperature visualization instead.
  • Air Quality Model Runs: this story uses NASA's PM2.5 (fine dust) model visualization.

The Delhi Air Story timeline itself uses Meteomatics weather and air quality readings, not NASA data.

Use of Super Intelligence (SI)

Our team used Super Intelligence (SI) tools to accelerate research, software development, and documentation.

  • Perplexity was used for technical research, API documentation, and Earth science resource discovery.
  • ChatGPT assisted with system architecture, software design, debugging, documentation, prompt engineering, and code refinement.
  • Lovable.dev accelerated frontend development by scaffolding the React application, generating UI components, and rapidly iterating on application features.

All scientific decisions, application design, engineering choices, environmental data selection, sonification methodology, implementation, testing, and validation were performed and approved by our team. No AI-generated environmental or NASA data was used. Environmental observations are retrieved from the Meteomatics Weather API, while NASA Earth Information Center resources provide scientific context and visualization. All audio is procedurally synthesized in real time using Tone.js from measured environmental variables rather than generated by AI.
